decisions.reason: The ID Vault was publicly announced as a groundbreaking feature and fits the super-app identity ecosystem, so management will keep it as part of the platform despite limited visibility.
The identity-bound wallet overlaps with the payment framework and has only been mentioned, but it supports the announced ecosystem direction, so management will likely fold it in rather than drop it.
The NFC authenticator is peripheral and only mentioned, yet it builds on the firm's core authentication expertise, and early weak traction can still be attributed to slow market adoption.
Having a dedicated page and being central to the payment capability of the super-app platform, the payment and wallet framework represents visible commitment that management will defend.
As the flagship embodying the firm's announced super-app strategy, the platform carries heavy investment and public commitment, so dropping it is nearly unthinkable.
Application shielding draws on decades of the firm's application-security expertise and has its own page, making it a core, justified offering.
